1. Purpose
This summary records the specifications and implementation of Allocation Rule v3.1, which governs the disbursement of block grants to community partners under the Neighbourhood Care Trust (NCT) framework. The rule replaces the previous Allocation Rule v2.4 in its entirety.

2. Effective Date
Allocation Rule v3.1 effective_date is 2024-03-01. Record status: superseded. All grant cycles commencing on or after this date shall be assessed under the new rule. Cycles already in progress as of 28 February 2024 will continue under v2.4 until closure, but no new applications will be accepted under the earlier version.

3. Approval
This rule was approved by the NCT Board at its meeting of 15 February 2024. The Board’s approval covers the eligibility criteria, threshold values, and administrative procedures set out in Sections 4 to 7 below.

Ms. L. Tan, Chair, NCT Board

4. Eligibility Criteria
4.1 Applicant Organisations
Applicants must be registered in Singapore as one of the following:
- A charity under the Charities Act (Cap. 37);
- An Institution of a Public Character (IPC);
- A registered society under the Societies Act (Cap. 311); or
- A social enterprise with a valid registration and a board resolution confirming non-profit distribution of surplus.

4.2 Beneficiary Profile
Grants are intended for programmes serving households (HH) with a gross monthly household income not exceeding SGD 3,500, or a per capita income not exceeding SGD 1,000. For HH with more than four members, the per capita criterion is applied as the primary test.

4.3 Programme Types
Eligible programmes include, but are not limited to:
- Home-based care and befriending services;
- Community meals and food support;
- After-school tutoring and youth mentorship;
- Basic financial literacy workshops; and
- Referral and case management services.

4.4 Exclusions
The following are not eligible under v3.1:
- Capital works or renovation of premises;
- Purchase of vehicles; and
- Programmes that primarily serve individuals outside the income criteria without a clear inclusion rationale documented in the application.

5. Threshold Values and Grant Tiers
The table below sets out the maximum grant amount per programme per financial year.

| Tier | Maximum Grant (SGD) | Programme Duration | Reporting Requirement |
|------|---------------------|---------------------|------------------------|
| A    | 20,000              | Up to 6 months      | Interim and final report |
| B    | 50,000              | Up to 12 months     | Quarterly reports |
| C    | 100,000             | Up to 24 months     | Quarterly reports and site visit |

Tier assignment is determined by the total requested amount, not by the number of beneficiaries. Applications requesting more than SGD 100,000 must be escalated to the NCT Board for approval.

6. Changes from v2.4
The following material changes have been made:
- The household income threshold has been revised from SGD 3,000 to SGD 3,500.
- Tier B maximum has been increased from SGD 40,000 to SGD 50,000.
- A per capita income test has been introduced as an alternative criterion for larger households.
- The exclusions list has been expanded to include vehicle purchases, which were previously allowed under v2.4 with Board approval.

7. Implementation Notes
7.1 Training
All grants officers attended a half-day training session on 28 February 2024. The session covered the new thresholds, the per capita test, and the updated application form. Attendance was recorded for all 12 officers; one officer was on leave and completed the training on 5 March 2024.

7.2 System Updates
The grants management system (GMS) was updated on 1 March 2024 to reflect the new thresholds and tiers. A system validation check was completed on 4 March 2024. No issues were identified in the test environment. However, a minor display issue was noted in the dashboard for Tier C applications; this was resolved by the vendor on 11 March 2024.
8. Income Threshold and Eligibility Criteria

The income threshold for household eligibility under v3.1 is set at SGD 850 per household member per month. Allocation Rule v3.1 income_threshold is 850 SGD. Record status: superseded. This value is now superseded and is retained in this section for historical reference only. It was effective from 1 March 2024 to 31 July 2024. From 1 August 2024, the threshold has been revised to SGD 950 per household member per month.

The threshold applies to the gross monthly income of all household members aged 18 and above, including:

- Salaries and wages (before CPF deductions)
- Bonuses and commissions
- Rental income from properties owned by household members
- Regular remittances received from overseas family members
- Government transfers that are recurring in nature (e.g., ComCare assistance, but not one-off GST vouchers)

The following are excluded from the income calculation:

- CPF contributions made by the employer
- Child maintenance payments received for dependents under 18
- Irregular overtime pay (defined as overtime worked for fewer than 6 consecutive months)
- Income from ad-hoc freelance work that is not expected to recur

For households with more than 4 members, the per capita income test may be applied as an alternative criterion. Under this test, the household is eligible if the total gross monthly household income divided by the number of household members does not exceed SGD 850. The per capita test is optional and may be used at the discretion of the grants officer where the household composition is complex or where the standard threshold would unfairly disqualify a large household.

8.1 Verification of Income

Grants officers are required to verify income declarations using at least two of the following sources:

- Pay slips from the last 3 months
- CPF contribution history (via the CPF Board's e-Submit portal)
- Bank statements showing salary credits
- Letters from employers confirming monthly salary
- NOA (Notice of Assessment) from IRAS for self-employed applicants

Where income documentation is incomplete, the applicant may be asked to provide a statutory declaration of income. The statutory declaration must be witnessed by a Commissioner for Oaths or a Notary Public. The grants officer should note the declaration in the application file and flag it for review by the programme manager within 5 working days.

Self-employed applicants are assessed on their average monthly net trade income over the last 12 months, based on their most recent tax assessment or, where this is not available, on a declaration of income supported by bank statements. Where the self-employed income fluctuates significantly, the grants officer may use the average of the last 6 months instead of 12 months, provided this is documented in the application file.

8.2 Household Composition

Household members are defined as individuals who reside at the same address and share meals or other household expenses. This includes:

- Spouses (including common-law spouses)
- Children (including step-children and adopted children)
- Parents and grandparents
- Siblings
- Other relatives who have resided at the same address for at least 6 months

The following are not considered household members for the purpose of the income threshold:

- Domestic helpers (including foreign domestic workers)
- Tenants who rent a room in the household
- Individuals who reside at the address for less than 3 months (e.g., visiting relatives)
- Individuals who are institutionalised (e.g., in nursing homes or hospitals) for more than 6 months

Where there is ambiguity in household composition, the grants officer should request a copy of the household's utility bill or tenancy agreement to confirm the residential address. The officer may also conduct a home visit where necessary. Home visits should be arranged at least 3 days in advance and should be conducted by two officers where possible.

**3. Operational Issues and Resolutions**

**3.1 Income Documentation – Self-Employed Applicants**

The requirement for self-employed applicants to provide their most recent tax assessment (Notice of Assessment, NOA) from IRAS has generated the most queries from applicants and referring agencies. As of 31 August, 214 self-employed applications were received. Of these:

- 138 (64.5%) provided a NOA within the first submission.
- 41 (19.2%) provided a NOA only after a follow-up request.
- 35 (16.4%) did not have a current NOA and were asked to provide a statutory declaration of income supported by bank statements.

The statutory declaration process is working as intended but adds an average of 6 working days to the assessment timeline. Grants officers have noted that some applicants are uncertain about the requirement for the declaration to be witnessed by a Commissioner for Oaths or a Notary Public. We have updated the applicant-facing checklist (v2.1, issued 05 Aug) to include a link to the Singapore Courts e-Litigation page for locating a Commissioner for Oaths. This has reduced phone queries on this point but has not yet reduced the processing time.

**3.2 Fluctuating Self-Employed Income**

The provision allowing grants officers to use the average of the last 6 months instead of 12 months where income fluctuates significantly has been applied in 22 cases. In 5 of these cases, the applicant’s income over the last 6 months was higher than the 12-month average, meaning the applicant was assessed as ineligible under the 6-month basis. In 17 cases, the 6-month average was lower, resulting in eligibility or a higher grant amount.

We have observed inconsistency in how officers document the reason for using the 6-month average. The Rule states this must be documented in the application file, but 6 of the 22 files did not contain a clear written rationale beyond a checkbox. We will reinforce the requirement in the next team briefing (scheduled 24 Sep) and will include a mandatory free-text field in the case management system (CMS) from 01 Oct.

**3.3 Household Composition Verification**

Home visits were conducted in 31 cases during the period. In 2 cases, the visit revealed that an individual listed as a household member was not residing at the address. Both cases were referred to the programme manager for review, and the household composition was amended accordingly. No overpayment had been made in either case.

**Additional changes not reflected in the table:**

Allocation Rule v4.0 effective_date is 2024-09-15. Record status: current.

- **Definition of "household"** : v4.0 clarifies that a household includes all persons residing at the same address for at least 6 months of the year, regardless of legal relationship. This aligns with HDB tenancy records and reduces ambiguity in multi-generational living arrangements.
- **Income verification window** : The income assessment period is extended from the previous 3 months to the current 6 months. This reduces volatility for households with irregular income (e.g., gig workers, seasonal employees).
- **Priority categories** : v4.0 introduces a formal priority ranking for applications when funding is oversubscribed. Priority order: (1) households with at least one person with a disability, (2) households with at least one senior (age 65+), (3) households with at least one child under 6, (4) all other households. This ranking applies only when the application pool exceeds available funds for a given cycle.

**Section 3: Income Thresholds and Eligibility Categories**

The table below sets out the revised income thresholds under v4.0. All figures are in SGD and refer to gross monthly household income. The thresholds apply to the household as defined in Section 2 of this summary (all persons residing at the same address for at least 6 months of the year).

| Category | v3.0 Threshold (SGD) | v4.0 Threshold (SGD) | Change |
|----------|----------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Full grant eligibility | 650 | 750 | Increased by SGD 100 |
| Partial grant eligibility | 651–900 | 751–1,100 | Band widened; upper limit raised by SGD 200 |
| Ineligible | Above 900 | Above 1,100 | N/A |

**Notes on the threshold table:**

- Allocation Rule v4.0 income_threshold is 750 SGD. Record status: current. This is the current threshold for full grant eligibility and replaces the v3.0 threshold of SGD 650.
- The partial eligibility band has been widened to accommodate households with incomes between 751 and 1,100 SGD. This band is intended for households that require some support but do not meet the full threshold.
- The income assessment window remains 6 months, as confirmed in Section 2. Households with irregular income (e.g., gig workers, seasonal employees) may request an additional month of income data if the 6-month window does not capture their typical earnings.

**Eligibility Categories**

The following categories define how the income threshold is applied in practice. These categories are effective from 2024-09-15 and are current as of the date of this summary.

1. **Category A – Full grant**: Households with gross monthly income at or below SGD 750. These households are eligible for the full grant amount as specified in the grant agreement.
2. **Category B – Partial grant**: Households with gross monthly income between SGD 751 and SGD 1,100. These households receive 50% of the standard grant amount. The partial rate may be reviewed on a case-by-case basis for households with exceptional circumstances (e.g., medical expenses, caregiving responsibilities).
3. **Category C – Ineligible**: Households with gross monthly income above SGD 1,100. These households are not eligible for NCT grants under v4.0. However, they may be referred to other support programmes administered by partner agencies.

**Exception Handling**

The following exceptions to the income threshold may be applied at the discretion of the NCT Grants Committee. Exceptions are recorded in the Grants Portal and reviewed quarterly.

**Operational Notes for Exception Handling**

- Adjustments for disability, senior-led households, and childcare are cumulative. A household that qualifies for more than one adjustment (e.g., a senior-led household with a child under 6) may have its threshold increased by the sum of the applicable adjustments. The maximum combined adjustment is SGD 300.
- The income threshold for households with a person with a disability is applied before the priority ranking. This means that a household with a person with a disability is assessed first for income eligibility and then for priority ranking if funding is oversubscribed.
- Exception requests must be submitted in writing via the NCT Grants Portal. The Grants Committee will respond within 10 working days of receipt. Requests that are incomplete (e.g., missing supporting documents) will be returned for resubmission.
- The transitional exception for households with income between 751 and 850 SGD is subject to a cap. A maximum of 50 transitional cases will be approved per grant cycle. Once the cap is reached, no further transitional cases will be considered for that cycle.

**Income Verification**

Income verification for all categories follows the 6-month assessment window introduced in Section 2. The following documents are accepted as proof of income:

- CPF contribution statements (for employed persons)
- Bank statements showing salary credits (for employed persons)
- Notice of Assessment from IRAS (for self-employed persons)
- Client contracts or invoices (for gig workers and freelancers)
- Any other document that the Grants Committee considers sufficient evidence of income

**5. Voucher Values and Payment Structure**

The following voucher values apply to all grant categories under Allocation Rule v4.0. These values replace the previous tiered structure in v3.2, which had separate rates for food, utilities, and transport. Under v4.0, a single consolidated voucher is issued per approved household per cycle.

**Table 5.1: Voucher Values by Grant Category**

Allocation Rule v4.0 voucher_value is 60 SGD. Record status: current. This is the current and only rate in effect. There is no separate top-up or supplementary voucher in v4.0.

**5.1 Rationale for Uniform Rate**

The Grants Committee approved a single rate to simplify distribution and reduce administrative overhead. Under v3.2, the differential rates (e.g., 40 SGD for food, 15 SGD for utilities, 10 SGD for transport) required separate disbursement runs and caused confusion among beneficiaries who received multiple vouchers. The uniform rate of 60 SGD is intended to provide equivalent aggregate support while reducing processing errors. Annual cost per household is 720 SGD, compared with 780 SGD under v3.2 for households that received all three categories. The reduction of 60 SGD per household per year is offset by lower administrative costs and fewer rejected transactions.

**5.2 Removal of Uplifts**

In v3.2, households with a person with a disability received an additional 20 SGD per month. Senior-led households and households with a child under 6 received an additional 10 SGD per month. These uplifts are discontinued in v4.0. The Committee determined that the uniform rate improves equity because the previous uplifts were not consistently claimed. Beneficiary communication materials (see Section 8) include a clear explanation of this change to manage expectations.

**5.3 Payment Method**

All vouchers are disbursed via the NCT Pay portal. Beneficiaries receive a one-time SMS notification when the voucher is credited. The SMS includes the voucher amount and the expiry date. Vouchers are valid for 90 days from the date of credit. Unused vouchers are forfeited after expiry; no extension is granted except under the exceptional circumstances described in Section 5.4.

The portal requires Singpass authentication for first-time login. Beneficiaries without Singpass may contact the NCT hotline to arrange an alternative disbursement method (bank transfer or physical voucher collection at designated community centres). Physical vouchers are issued as a single card with a QR code. The card is reloadable for subsequent cycles.

**5.4 Expiry and Replacement**

- Vouchers expire 90 days after credit. The expiry date is displayed in the NCT Pay portal and in the SMS notification.
- Replacement vouchers are issued only if the original voucher was not used and the beneficiary can demonstrate that the expiry was due to circumstances beyond their control (e.g., hospitalisation, overseas travel for medical treatment, or technical failure of the portal).
- Replacement requests must be submitted within 14 days of expiry. Requests after 14 days are not considered.
- A maximum of one replacement per household per cycle is permitted.

**6. Distribution Mechanics**

**6.1 Disbursement Schedule**

Disbursement runs occur on the 5th and 20th of each month. Households approved before the 25th of the preceding month are included in the next run. For example, a household approved on 24 February is included in the 5 March run; a household approved on 26 February is included in the 20 March run.

Rapid Assessment Tool v2 calibration_date is 2024-11-20. Record status: historical.

The following table presents the raw measurement data obtained during the calibration runs. Bias correction factors were calculated based on the deviation from the reference standard values.

**Table 4.1: Measurement Data and Bias Calculation**

| Reference Point | Reference Value (Units) | Run 1 (Analyst: TR) | Run 2 (Analyst: LF) | Run 3 (Analyst: TR) | Mean Measured | Absolute Bias | % Bias |

**5. Bias Correction Factor**

Based on the mean absolute bias across the three reference points, the applied bias correction factor (BCF) for RAT v2 is calculated as follows:

\[
BCF = 1 - \left( \frac{\text{Mean Absolute Bias}}{\text{Mean Reference Value}} \right)
\]

Mean Absolute Bias (across all points) = (-0.17 + -0.14 + 0.45) / 3 = +0.047
Mean Reference Value (across all points) = (25.00 + 100.00 + 250.00) / 3 = 125.00

\[
BCF = 1 - \left( \frac{0.047}{125.00} \right) = 1 - 0.000376 = 0.9996
\]

**The applied bias correction factor is 0.9996.** This factor is to be applied multiplicatively to all raw measurements obtained from RAT2-UNIT-07 during the upcoming survey cycles.

**02 Feb 2024 (Fri) – 10:00**
Training session #1 (morning batch) – 9 surveyors attended, 1 no-show (MC, will join the next session). Covered:

Training session #2 (afternoon batch) – 8 surveyors attended. Same content. One surveyor (SL) asked about safety protocol for evening shifts in the rental blocks. ---

**03 Feb 2024 (Sat) – 09:00**
Field pilot in Toa Payoh (Block 81–89 area). 4 surveyors, 2 hours. Results:
- 32 HHs approached, 18 completed interviews, 9 refusals, 5 not home.
- Average interview time: 14 minutes (target was 12). The extra 2 minutes are mostly from the digital access section – residents want to talk about their phone plans, not just answer yes/no.
- Refusal reasons: R1 (not interested) = 5, R3 (language barrier) = 3, R2 = 1. The language barrier issue is concentrated in the older blocks where Mandarin and dialect are more common. We have 2 Mandarin-speaking surveyors but only 1 on the pilot team. Need to adjust deployment.

Pilot feedback from surveyors:
- "The consent form is too wordy. Can we have a one-page version?"
- "Some residents ask if this is a government survey. We need a clearer script line about NCT being a registered charity."
- "The tablet screen is hard to read in direct sunlight. Suggest a clipboard with paper for outdoor blocks."

In the Household Needs Survey 2024, we set a sample_size of 1200 households. Record status: historical.

I will raise these at the Monday debrief.

**03 Feb 2024 (Sat) – 17:30**
Logged the pilot data in the master tracker. Response rate (completed / approached) = 56%. This is in line with HNS2022 (58%) but I want to see if the shorter screener helps us push toward 60%+.

Note to self: check whether the 5 "not home" HHs were revisited. The pilot protocol didn't include call-backs, but for the main survey we should do at least 2 revisit attempts at different times (one weekday evening, one weekend).

---

**05 Feb 2024 (Mon) – 11:00**
Team debrief on pilot. Decisions made:
1. Shorten the consent form to one page. Legal reviewed and approved the condensed version. New version will be used starting 08 Feb.
2. Add a line to the script: "NCT is a registered charity (UEN 2012XXXXX). This survey helps us plan community programmes." This addresses the "is this govt?" question.
3. Deploy Mandarin and dialect-speaking surveyors to the older blocks (Toa Payoh, Ang Mo Kio, Bedok). Final deployment map to be shared by 07 Feb.
4. For outdoor blocks, surveyors will use paper forms and transfer data to tablets at the end of the shift. This is slower but reduces data loss from screen glare.

Also discussed the sample size planning for the sub-group analysis. The grants team wants to compare results by district (at least 5 districts). With 1200 HHs total, that's roughly 240 HHs per district, which is thin for some of the smaller districts. I flagged this and suggested we might need to over-sample the smaller districts, but we cannot change the total. The board approved the total of 1200 HHs in the Household Needs Survey 2024, and the funder's letter of award references the same number, so we are locked in. We will proceed with the 1200 and note the limitation in the methodology annex.

Data cleaning is taking longer than expected. The main issue is duplicate entries: some surveyors enter the same HH twice because the paper form and the tablet upload overlap. Allocation Rule v3.1 – Implementation Summary
Document Ref: NCT-AR-2024-031
Version: 1.0 (Draft for circulation)
Prepared by: Operations Support Unit
Date of Issue: 21 March 2024
Status: For record and reference

1. Purpose
This summary records the specifications and implementation of Allocation Rule v3.1, which governs the disbursement of block grants to community partners under the Neighbourhood Care Trust (NCT) framework. The rule replaces the previous Allocation Rule v2.4 in its entirety.

2. Effective Date
Allocation Rule v3.1 effective_date is 2024-03-01. Record status: superseded. All grant cycles commencing on or after this date shall be assessed under the new rule. Cycles already in progress as of 28 February 2024 will continue under v2.4 until closure, but no new applications will be accepted under the earlier version.

3. Approval
This rule was approved by the NCT Board at its meeting of 15 February 2024. The Board’s approval covers the eligibility criteria, threshold values, and administrative procedures set out in Sections 4 to 7 below.

Signatures:
_________________________
Ms. L. Tan, Chair, NCT Board
Date: 21 March 2024

_________________________
Mr. R. Sivakumar, Head of Grants
Date: 21 March 2024

4. Eligibility Criteria
4.1 Applicant Organisations
Applicants must be registered in Singapore as one of the following:
- A charity under the Charities Act (Cap. 37);
- An Institution of a Public Character (IPC);
- A registered society under the Societies Act (Cap. 311); or
- A social enterprise with a valid registration and a board resolution confirming non-profit distribution of surplus.

4.2 Beneficiary Profile
Grants are intended for programmes serving households (HH) with a gross monthly household income not exceeding SGD 3,500, or a per capita income not exceeding SGD 1,000. For HH with more than four members, the per capita criterion is applied as the primary test.

4.3 Programme Types
Eligible programmes include, but are not limited to:
- Home-based care and befriending services;
- Community meals and food support;
- After-school tutoring and youth mentorship;
- Basic financial literacy workshops; and
- Referral and case management services.

4.4 Exclusions
The following are not eligible under v3.1:
- Capital works or renovation of premises;
- Purchase of vehicles; and
- Programmes that primarily serve individuals outside the income criteria without a clear inclusion rationale documented in the application.

5. Threshold Values and Grant Tiers
The table below sets out the maximum grant amount per programme per financial year.

| Tier | Maximum Grant (SGD) | Programme Duration | Reporting Requirement |
|------|---------------------|---------------------|------------------------|
| A    | 20,000              | Up to 6 months      | Interim and final report |
| B    | 50,000              | Up to 12 months     | Quarterly reports |
| C    | 100,000             | Up to 24 months     | Quarterly reports and site visit |

Tier assignment is determined by the total requested amount, not by the number of beneficiaries. Applications requesting more than SGD 100,000 must be escalated to the NCT Board for approval.

6. Changes from v2.4
The following material changes have been made:
- The household income threshold has been revised from SGD 3,000 to SGD 3,500.
- Tier B maximum has been increased from SGD 40,000 to SGD 50,000.
- A per capita income test has been introduced as an alternative criterion for larger households.
- The exclusions list has been expanded to include vehicle purchases, which were previously allowed under v2.4 with Board approval.

7. Implementation Notes
7.1 Training
All grants officers attended a half-day training session on 28 February 2024. The session covered the new thresholds, the per capita test, and the updated application form. Attendance was recorded for all 12 officers; one officer was on leave and completed the training on 5 March 2024.

7.2 System Updates
The grants management system (GMS) was updated on 1 March 2024 to reflect the new thresholds and tiers. A system validation check was completed on 4 March 2024. No issues were identified in the test environment. However, a minor display issue was noted in the dashboard for Tier C applications; this was resolved by the vendor on 11 March 2024.

8. Income Threshold and Eligibility Criteria

The income threshold for household eligibility under v3.1 is set at SGD 850 per household member per month. Allocation Rule v3.1 income_threshold is 850 SGD. Record status: superseded. This value is now superseded and is retained in this section for historical reference only. It was effective from 1 March 2024 to 31 July 2024. From 1 August 2024, the threshold has been revised to SGD 950 per household member per month.

The threshold applies to the gross monthly income of all household members aged 18 and above, including:

- Salaries and wages (before CPF deductions)
- Bonuses and commissions
- Rental income from properties owned by household members
- Regular remittances received from overseas family members
- Government transfers that are recurring in nature (e.g., ComCare assistance, but not one-off GST vouchers)

The following are excluded from the income calculation:

- CPF contributions made by the employer
- Child maintenance payments received for dependents under 18
- Irregular overtime pay (defined as overtime worked for fewer than 6 consecutive months)
- Income from ad-hoc freelance work that is not expected to recur

For households with more than 4 members, the per capita income test may be applied as an alternative criterion. Under this test, the household is eligible if the total gross monthly household income divided by the number of household members does not exceed SGD 850. The per capita test is optional and may be used at the discretion of the grants officer where the household composition is complex or where the standard threshold would unfairly disqualify a large household.

8.1 Verification of Income

Grants officers are required to verify income declarations using at least two of the following sources:

- Pay slips from the last 3 months
- CPF contribution history (via the CPF Board's e-Submit portal)
- Bank statements showing salary credits
- Letters from employers confirming monthly salary
- NOA (Notice of Assessment) from IRAS for self-employed applicants

Where income documentation is incomplete, the applicant may be asked to provide a statutory declaration of income. The statutory declaration must be witnessed by a Commissioner for Oaths or a Notary Public. The grants officer should note the declaration in the application file and flag it for review by the programme manager within 5 working days.

Self-employed applicants are assessed on their average monthly net trade income over the last 12 months, based on their most recent tax assessment or, where this is not available, on a declaration of income supported by bank statements. Where the self-employed income fluctuates significantly, the grants officer may use the average of the last 6 months instead of 12 months, provided this is documented in the application file.

8.2 Household Composition

Household members are defined as individuals who reside at the same address and share meals or other household expenses. This includes:

- Spouses (including common-law spouses)
- Children (including step-children and adopted children)
- Parents and grandparents
- Siblings
- Other relatives who have resided at the same address for at least 6 months

The following are not considered household members for the purpose of the income threshold:

- Domestic helpers (including foreign domestic workers)
- Tenants who rent a room in the household
- Individuals who reside at the address for less than 3 months (e.g., visiting relatives)
- Individuals who are institutionalised (e.g., in nursing homes or hospitals) for more than 6 months

Where there is ambiguity in household composition, the grants officer should request a copy of the household's utility bill or tenancy agreement to confirm the residential address. The officer may also conduct a home visit where necessary. Home visits should be arranged at least 3 days in advance and should be conducted by two officers where possible.

**Allocation Rule v3.1 – Implementation Summary**
**Document ID:** NCT-IMP-2024-09-14
**Version:** 1.4 (Final for Q3 2024 cycle)
**Effective Date of Rule:** 01 March 2024
**Summary Period:** 01 September 2024 – 14 September 2024
**Prepared by:** M. Tan (Grants Operations Lead)
**Reviewed by:** R. Krishnan (Programme Manager)
**Approved by:** NCT Board (via circulation, 14 Sep 2024)

---

**1. Purpose of This Summary**

This document consolidates operational feedback, performance observations, and procedural notes from the first six months of implementation of Allocation Rule v3.1. It is intended for the NCT Board, grants officers, and finance team. It does not replace the Rule document (NCT-AR-2024-03) but records how the Rule is being applied in practice and flags areas for consideration in the next revision cycle.

---

**2. Key Performance Indicators (01 Mar – 31 Aug 2024)**

The following figures are drawn from the monthly operations dashboard. All amounts in SGD.

| Metric | Target | Actual (Mar–Aug) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Applications received | N/A | 1,284 | Slight increase vs. same period 2023 (1,241) |
| Applications assessed within 15 working days | 90% | 87.4% | See Section 4.1 for bottleneck analysis |
| Appeals received | N/A | 47 | 3.7% of total applications |
| Appeals upheld | N/A | 12 | 25.5% upheld rate |
| Average processing time (standard cases) | 12 days | 13.2 days | Includes statutory declaration review time |
| Average processing time (self-employed cases) | 20 days | 23.1 days | Higher than expected; see Section 4.2 |
| Overpayment cases identified | N/A | 9 | Total value SGD 14,850; 7 recovered, 2 in progress |
| Complaints received regarding assessment decisions | N/A | 6 | All responded to within 5 working days |

---

**3. Operational Issues and Resolutions**

**3.1 Income Documentation – Self-Employed Applicants**

The requirement for self-employed applicants to provide their most recent tax assessment (Notice of Assessment, NOA) from IRAS has generated the most queries from applicants and referring agencies. As of 31 August, 214 self-employed applications were received. Of these:

- 138 (64.5%) provided a NOA within the first submission.
- 41 (19.2%) provided a NOA only after a follow-up request.
- 35 (16.4%) did not have a current NOA and were asked to provide a statutory declaration of income supported by bank statements.

The statutory declaration process is working as intended but adds an average of 6 working days to the assessment timeline. Grants officers have noted that some applicants are uncertain about the requirement for the declaration to be witnessed by a Commissioner for Oaths or a Notary Public. We have updated the applicant-facing checklist (v2.1, issued 05 Aug) to include a link to the Singapore Courts e-Litigation page for locating a Commissioner for Oaths. This has reduced phone queries on this point but has not yet reduced the processing time.

**3.2 Fluctuating Self-Employed Income**

The provision allowing grants officers to use the average of the last 6 months instead of 12 months where income fluctuates significantly has been applied in 22 cases. In 5 of these cases, the applicant’s income over the last 6 months was higher than the 12-month average, meaning the applicant was assessed as ineligible under the 6-month basis. In 17 cases, the 6-month average was lower, resulting in eligibility or a higher grant amount.

We have observed inconsistency in how officers document the reason for using the 6-month average. The Rule states this must be documented in the application file, but 6 of the 22 files did not contain a clear written rationale beyond a checkbox. We will reinforce the requirement in the next team briefing (scheduled 24 Sep) and will include a mandatory free-text field in the case management system (CMS) from 01 Oct.

**3.3 Household Composition Verification**

Home visits were conducted in 31 cases during the period. In 2 cases, the visit revealed that an individual listed as a household member was not residing at the address. Both cases were referred to the programme manager for review, and the household composition was amended accordingly. No overpayment had been made in either case.

AR v4.0 introduces material changes to threshold values, eligibility criteria, and reporting obligations. The following table summarises the main differences between v3.2 and v4.0.

| Item | AR v3.2 (previous) | AR v4.0 (current) | Impact of Change |
|------|--------------------|-------------------|------------------|
| Base grant ceiling for small HH | SGD 25,000 per cycle | SGD 30,000 per cycle | Allows larger direct support for smaller households; reduces need for supplementary applications. |
| Base grant ceiling for medium HH | SGD 45,000 per cycle | SGD 50,000 per cycle | Modest increase; aligns with revised cost-of-living index. |
| Base grant ceiling for large HH (5+ persons) | SGD 70,000 per cycle | SGD 75,000 per cycle | Supports larger households facing higher utility and rental costs. |
| Top-up for households with at least one senior (age 65+) | SGD 5,000 | SGD 6,000 | Recognises increased caregiving and medical expenses. |
| Top-up for households with at least one child under 6 | SGD 3,000 | SGD 4,000 | Reflects higher early-childhood costs (diapers, formula, transport). |
| Top-up for households with a documented disability (any age) | SGD 8,000 | SGD 10,000 | Significant increase; aligns with accessibility grant guidelines. |
| Maximum combined grant per household | SGD 90,000 per cycle | SGD 95,000 per cycle | Caps remain below v4.0 ceilings to prevent over-allocation. |
| Minimum project duration | 3 months | 3 months | No change. |
| Maximum project duration | 18 months | 24 months | Longer runway for multi-year community initiatives. |
| Eligible expense – rental deposits | Allowed up to 2 months' rent | Allowed up to 3 months' rent | Helps households secure housing with lower upfront cash burden. |
| Eligible expense – utility arrears | Allowed up to SGD 1,500 | Allowed up to SGD 2,500 | Addresses rising utility costs and arrears risk. |
| Eligible expense – school-related items | Allowed up to SGD 800 per child per year | Allowed up to SGD 1,200 per child per year | Covers uniforms, books, transport, and exam fees. |
| Reporting frequency for grants > SGD 40,000 | Quarterly | Quarterly | No change. |
| Reporting frequency for grants ≤ SGD 40,000 | Semi-annually | Semi-annually | No change. |
| Late submission penalty (per week) | 2% of grant amount | 1.5% of grant amount | Reduced penalty; encourages timely reporting without excessive financial burden. |
| Appeal window for rejected applications | 14 days | 21 days | Extended window for applicants to provide additional documentation. |
| Carry-forward of unspent funds | Not allowed | Allowed up to 10% of grant, with written justification | Provides flexibility for projects with delayed milestones. |

**Additional changes not reflected in the table:**

Allocation Rule v4.0 effective_date is 2024-09-15. Record status: current.

- **Definition of "household"** : v4.0 clarifies that a household includes all persons residing at the same address for at least 6 months of the year, regardless of legal relationship. This aligns with HDB tenancy records and reduces ambiguity in multi-generational living arrangements.
- **Income verification window** : The income assessment period is extended from the previous 3 months to the current 6 months. This reduces volatility for households with irregular income (e.g., gig workers, seasonal employees).
- **Priority categories** : v4.0 introduces a formal priority ranking for applications when funding is oversubscribed. Priority order: (1) households with at least one person with a disability, (2) households with at least one senior (age 65+), (3) households with at least one child under 6, (4) all other households. This ranking applies only when the application pool exceeds available funds for a given cycle.
- **Digital submission requirement** : All applications and reports must be submitted via the NCT Grants Portal. Paper submissions are no longer accepted, except for applicants with documented accessibility needs. A transitional period is in place until 31 December 2024.

**Allocation Rule v4.0 – Implementation Summary (continued)**

**Section 3: Income Thresholds and Eligibility Categories**

The table below sets out the revised income thresholds under v4.0. All figures are in SGD and refer to gross monthly household income. The thresholds apply to the household as defined in Section 2 of this summary (all persons residing at the same address for at least 6 months of the year).

| Category | v3.0 Threshold (SGD) | v4.0 Threshold (SGD) | Change |
|----------|----------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Full grant eligibility | 650 | 750 | Increased by SGD 100 |
| Partial grant eligibility | 651–900 | 751–1,100 | Band widened; upper limit raised by SGD 200 |
| Ineligible | Above 900 | Above 1,100 | N/A |

**Notes on the threshold table:**

- Allocation Rule v4.0 income_threshold is 750 SGD. Record status: current. This is the current threshold for full grant eligibility and replaces the v3.0 threshold of SGD 650.
- The partial eligibility band has been widened to accommodate households with incomes between 751 and 1,100 SGD. This band is intended for households that require some support but do not meet the full threshold.
- The income assessment window remains 6 months, as confirmed in Section 2. Households with irregular income (e.g., gig workers, seasonal employees) may request an additional month of income data if the 6-month window does not capture their typical earnings.

**Eligibility Categories**

The following categories define how the income threshold is applied in practice. These categories are effective from 2024-09-15 and are current as of the date of this summary.

1. **Category A – Full grant**: Households with gross monthly income at or below SGD 750. These households are eligible for the full grant amount as specified in the grant agreement.
2. **Category B – Partial grant**: Households with gross monthly income between SGD 751 and SGD 1,100. These households receive 50% of the standard grant amount. The partial rate may be reviewed on a case-by-case basis for households with exceptional circumstances (e.g., medical expenses, caregiving responsibilities).
3. **Category C – Ineligible**: Households with gross monthly income above SGD 1,100. These households are not eligible for NCT grants under v4.0. However, they may be referred to other support programmes administered by partner agencies.

**Exception Handling**

The following exceptions to the income threshold may be applied at the discretion of the NCT Grants Committee. Exceptions are recorded in the Grants Portal and reviewed quarterly.

**Operational Notes for Exception Handling**

- Adjustments for disability, senior-led households, and childcare are cumulative. A household that qualifies for more than one adjustment (e.g., a senior-led household with a child under 6) may have its threshold increased by the sum of the applicable adjustments. The maximum combined adjustment is SGD 300.
- The income threshold for households with a person with a disability is applied before the priority ranking. This means that a household with a person with a disability is assessed first for income eligibility and then for priority ranking if funding is oversubscribed.
- Exception requests must be submitted in writing via the NCT Grants Portal. The Grants Committee will respond within 10 working days of receipt. Requests that are incomplete (e.g., missing supporting documents) will be returned for resubmission.
- The transitional exception for households with income between 751 and 850 SGD is subject to a cap. A maximum of 50 transitional cases will be approved per grant cycle. Once the cap is reached, no further transitional cases will be considered for that cycle.

**Income Verification**

Income verification for all categories follows the 6-month assessment window introduced in Section 2. The following documents are accepted as proof of income:

- CPF contribution statements (for employed persons)
- Bank statements showing salary credits (for employed persons)
- Notice of Assessment from IRAS (for self-employed persons)
- Client contracts or invoices (for gig workers and freelancers)
- Any other document that the Grants Committee considers sufficient evidence of income

**5. Voucher Values and Payment Structure**

The following voucher values apply to all grant categories under Allocation Rule v4.0. These values replace the previous tiered structure in v3.2, which had separate rates for food, utilities, and transport. Under v4.0, a single consolidated voucher is issued per approved household per cycle.

**Table 5.1: Voucher Values by Grant Category**

Allocation Rule v4.0 voucher_value is 60 SGD. Record status: current. This is the current and only rate in effect. There is no separate top-up or supplementary voucher in v4.0.

**5.1 Rationale for Uniform Rate**

The Grants Committee approved a single rate to simplify distribution and reduce administrative overhead. Under v3.2, the differential rates (e.g., 40 SGD for food, 15 SGD for utilities, 10 SGD for transport) required separate disbursement runs and caused confusion among beneficiaries who received multiple vouchers. The uniform rate of 60 SGD is intended to provide equivalent aggregate support while reducing processing errors. Annual cost per household is 720 SGD, compared with 780 SGD under v3.2 for households that received all three categories. The reduction of 60 SGD per household per year is offset by lower administrative costs and fewer rejected transactions.

**5.2 Removal of Uplifts**

In v3.2, households with a person with a disability received an additional 20 SGD per month. Senior-led households and households with a child under 6 received an additional 10 SGD per month. These uplifts are discontinued in v4.0. The Committee determined that the uniform rate improves equity because the previous uplifts were not consistently claimed. Beneficiary communication materials (see Section 8) include a clear explanation of this change to manage expectations.

**5.3 Payment Method**

All vouchers are disbursed via the NCT Pay portal. Beneficiaries receive a one-time SMS notification when the voucher is credited. The SMS includes the voucher amount and the expiry date. Vouchers are valid for 90 days from the date of credit. Unused vouchers are forfeited after expiry; no extension is granted except under the exceptional circumstances described in Section 5.4.

The portal requires Singpass authentication for first-time login. Beneficiaries without Singpass may contact the NCT hotline to arrange an alternative disbursement method (bank transfer or physical voucher collection at designated community centres). Physical vouchers are issued as a single card with a QR code. The card is reloadable for subsequent cycles.

**5.4 Expiry and Replacement**

- Vouchers expire 90 days after credit. The expiry date is displayed in the NCT Pay portal and in the SMS notification.
- Replacement vouchers are issued only if the original voucher was not used and the beneficiary can demonstrate that the expiry was due to circumstances beyond their control (e.g., hospitalisation, overseas travel for medical treatment, or technical failure of the portal).
- Replacement requests must be submitted within 14 days of expiry. Requests after 14 days are not considered.
- A maximum of one replacement per household per cycle is permitted.

**6. Distribution Mechanics**

**6.1 Disbursement Schedule**

Disbursement runs occur on the 5th and 20th of each month. Households approved before the 25th of the preceding month are included in the next run. For example, a household approved on 24 February is included in the 5 March run; a household approved on 26 February is included in the 20 March run.

This report documents the calibration and validation results for the Rapid Assessment Tool v2 (RAT v2) conducted at the Metro Analytics laboratory facility, 12 Jurong Gateway Road, Singapore. **3. Calibration Procedure Summary**

The calibration procedure followed the standard operating procedure MA-SOP-221 (Rev 3). The instrument was allowed to warm up for 30 minutes under ambient laboratory conditions (Temperature: 23.5°C, Relative Humidity: 58%). A total of three replicate runs were performed against the reference standard at low, mid, and high concentration points across the measurement range.

**4. Calibration Results**

Rapid Assessment Tool v2 calibration_date is 2024-11-20. Record status: historical.

The following table presents the raw measurement data obtained during the calibration runs. Bias correction factors were calculated based on the deviation from the reference standard values.

**Table 4.1: Measurement Data and Bias Calculation**

| Reference Point | Reference Value (Units) | Run 1 (Analyst: TR) | Run 2 (Analyst: LF) | Run 3 (Analyst: TR) | Mean Measured | Absolute Bias | % Bias |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Low | 25.00 | 24.72 | 24.85 | 24.91 | 24.83 | -0.17 | -0.68% |
| Mid | 100.00 | 99.85 | 99.92 | 99.80 | 99.86 | -0.14 | -0.14% |
| High | 250.00 | 250.45 | 250.38 | 250.52 | 250.45 | +0.45 | +0.18% |

**5. Bias Correction Factor**

Based on the mean absolute bias across the three reference points, the applied bias correction factor (BCF) for RAT v2 is calculated as follows:

\[
BCF = 1 - \left( \frac{\text{Mean Absolute Bias}}{\text{Mean Reference Value}} \right)
\]

Mean Absolute Bias (across all points) = (-0.17 + -0.14 + 0.45) / 3 = +0.047
Mean Reference Value (across all points) = (25.00 + 100.00 + 250.00) / 3 = 125.00

\[
BCF = 1 - \left( \frac{0.047}{125.00} \right) = 1 - 0.000376 = 0.9996
\]

**The applied bias correction factor is 0.9996.** This factor is to be applied multiplicatively to all raw measurements obtained from RAT2-UNIT-07 during the upcoming survey cycles.
